key_insight: Leakage-controlled branching motifs from longitudinal EHR graphs mainly improved long-range event timing, not overall disease-endpoint discrimination.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help researchers build more inspectable trajectory models for forecasting clinical events, but its value appears strongest for timing support rather than broad predictive superiority.
method: Split patients before graph construction to prevent leakage.
Learn train-only consecutive-admission transitions and freeze endpoint-specific branching policies chosen on validation data.
Use a time-aware Transformer with endpoint-specific cross-attention to retrieve up to 24 compatible motifs per endpoint.
evidence_signal: Across five seeds, micro-AUPRC rose from 0.9330 to 0.9357 and event-time MAE fell from 676.9 to 657.7 days, with larger gains for events occurring after 730 days.
watch_item: The motif-based gains were not uniformly better than a matched history-only model on survival metrics, so deployment should not assume better global prognostic performance.
paper_title: Graph-Enhanced Disease Trajectory Discovery and Temporal Endpoint Forecasting from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
